description: The `struct` declaration slot, without Sprites: `struct tell`/`ask`/`each` each raise `ol-reserved-word` under `["core-language", "data"]` — Sprites, which owns these three names, is not claimed; Data is present because `struct` is a Data-profile form. Same three names as `reserved-procedures-without-sprites` and deliberately so -- `spec/grammar.md:165` makes `define`/`to` and `struct` separate declaration slots, so this pins that the built-in-names rule reaches BOTH, and a fix applied to procedure declarations alone leaves this fixture red. HISTORY: issue #679 wrote it as the OFF half of a profile gate, expecting three clean declarations; ruling #833 retracted the gate, issue #855 aligned `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:154`, and issue #841 removed the gate from the checker, so the expectation is flipped here rather than the fixture deleted. `"check": true`: checker diagnostics only -- no struct is ever instantiated and no events are produced. `message` is deliberately absent from the diagnostics below: the harness strips it from BOTH sides before comparing (`scripts/harness/index.mjs:977-983` projects every diagnostic to code/span/params/stage/severity), so a `message` here would be an assertion nothing can evaluate -- measured on one of these six by asserting a deliberately WRONG message, which the suite still accepted. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and "prose is presentation" (`spec/error-model.md:253`); the learner-facing wording is pinned by unit tests instead. The twin DOES carry `message`, and that asymmetry is intentional rather than an oversight; dropping the decorative field from the twins is a corpus-wide edit and belongs to issue #842.
